about: Held-out probes on 9 chemical-engineering papers chosen by the rule in PLAN.md (PMC open-access, 2026), written from each paper's pdftotext text (plain and -layout; not its clause base, not ugrc's atoms, not any model answer) before any run, 2026-10-30. cat, as in experiments/new6/probes.json: C lookup, B binding trap (a near value for another entity is printed nearby), T table, X computation, H chained lookup, F false premise, A absence. expect cites the paper's table or section. must: every group must occur in the answer (alternatives inside a group; NEG = any absence wording) - a triage aid only, every answer is graded by hand. Frozen by frozen.sha256 before the first run.

distillation.q: What boiling points do hydroquinone and catechol have at 10 kPa?
distillation.trap: normal boiling points 287.0 / 245.0 or the 30 kPa values 241.5 / 201.4

distillation.q: In the shortcut (DSTWU) column results, what were the minimum and actual reflux ratios and the minimum and actual numbers of trays?
distillation.expect: minimum reflux 1.325, actual 1.455; minimum 7 trays, actual 20 (feed tray 15) (Table 4)

distillation.q: With 18 theoretical trays and the feed on tray 13, what catechol mass fraction is obtained at the top of the column?
distillation.trap: neighbouring cells, e.g. 0.95317 (18 trays, feed 14) or 0.98644 (Table 10)

distillation.q: What bottom heat load does the column have with 16 theoretical trays and the feed on tray 15?
What optimal operating conditions did the study identify, and what purities and recoveries did they give?
distillation.expect: 10 kPa, 16 theoretical plates, feed on tray 11, mass reflux ratio 3.143, D/F 0.092; HQ purity 99.2%, CAT purity 99%, HQ recovery 98.5%, CAT recovery 97.8% (abstract)

distillation.q: By how many kJ/kg does the optimization reduce the total specific energy consumption, including the vacuum pumps?
What share of the optimized process's total specific energy consumption is the vacuum pump?
At the tray count and feed stage finally chosen as optimal, what hydroquinone mass fraction does the column bottom reach in the tray/feed study?
distillation.trap: the 20-tray value 0.99121 or the top catechol 0.98981

distillation.q: Why did the catechol purity at the column top fall when the operating pressure was lowered from 20 to 5 kPa?
distillation.expect: premise false: it ROSE from 0.94377 to 0.99996 (sec. 4.1)

distillation.q: Why did the optimization raise the distillate-to-feed ratio above the industrial baseline?
distillation.expect: premise false: D/F was REDUCED from 0.121 to 0.092 (abstract)

distillation.q: What column diameter does the optimized vacuum distillation design require?

adsorption.q: For a monolith dosage of 0.75 g and an initial dye concentration of 100 mg/L, what apparent rate constant and R2 does Table 1 report?
Which run of the Box-Behnken design gave the lowest decolorization efficiency, and under what conditions?
In the ANOVA, what F-value and p-value does the BC interaction term have?
What apparent optical band gap did the Cu2O-Ag@ACR/LF-3D monolith have?
adsorption.trap: the 2.0-2.2 eV literature range for Cu2O

adsorption.q: What optimum conditions did response surface methodology find, and what decolorization efficiency was predicted and then measured?
adsorption.expect: pH 5.94, 68.07 mg/L dye, 0.71 g monolith; predicted 98.14%, validated 96.43% (abstract)

adsorption.q: What is the mean decolorization efficiency of the Box-Behnken center-point runs (pH 6.0, 70 mg/L, 0.70 g)?
At 75 mg/L, by what factor is the apparent rate constant at a 1.0 g dosage larger than at 0.5 g?
What BET surface area was estimated for the material whose band gap was 1.99 eV?
adsorption.expect: Cu2O-Ag@ACR/LF-3D: 8.03 m2/g, a tentative estimate sensitive to the fitting range (N2 physisorption section)

adsorption.q: Why did the monolith keep its decolorization efficiency above 90% over five reuse cycles?
adsorption.expect: premise false: efficiency fell to 92.04, 85.86, 80.82, 74.31 and 63.62% over cycles 1-5 (about 66% retained); Cu release was a key limitation

adsorption.q: Why was the linear term for initial dye concentration the most significant term of the quadratic model?
adsorption.expect: premise false: the linear B term was not significant (p = 0.4196); pH (A) dominated, though B2 was significant (Table 3)

adsorption.q: What average pore diameter did the Cu2O-Ag@ACR/LF-3D monolith have?
adsorption.expect: not reported: the paper states pore-size distributions were not reliable enough and are not reported

reactor.q: At 20% NH3 blending, what CO concentration (ppm, 6% O2) was measured in the drop-tube test and what did the simulation give?
What ash content (as received) and net heating value does the Ordos lignite have?
Which reactor in the boiler's network receives the overfire air, and what is its role?
reactor.expect: C1-R5, Burnout Zone (OFA): further oxidation with overfire air, char burnout; inlets from R4 + OFA (Table 1)
reactor.trap: C1-R3 (70% secondary air) or C1-R4 reduction zone

reactor.q: What are the primary, secondary and burnout air rates and the excess air coefficient in the baseline air staging?
At 20% cofiring, what CO2, CO and NO changes does post-flame injection give, and what NO change does burnout-zone injection give?
reactor.expect: post-flame: CO2 -33%, CO -80%, NO about +88%; burnout zone: NO about +571% (abstract)

reactor.q: How many tonnes of coal per hour does 40% NH3 blending save compared with pure coal firing?
For pure coal firing, what is the relative error of the simulated NO concentration against the measured one?
What ammonia flow rate is used in the cofiring case whose coal feeding rate is 20.33 kg/s?
Why did NO emissions keep rising all the way up to 80% NH3 blending?
reactor.expect: premise false: NO rose from 20% to 60% but DECREASED at 80% (H/OH radical competition) (abstract)

reactor.q: Why did burnout-zone injection give the lowest NO of the 20% cofiring cases?
reactor.expect: premise false: flame-zone injection gives the lowest NO; burnout-zone injection gives the largest NO penalty (about +571%) (abstract)

reactor.q: What boiler thermal efficiency does the model predict at 40% NH3 cofiring?
reactor.expect: not reported (the paper reports outlet species, not boiler efficiency)

pyrolysis.q: According to Table 3, at which FTIR absorption peaks does CO2 appear under air and under nitrogen?
pyrolysis.expect: air: 670 and 2360 cm-1; nitrogen: 634 and 2315 cm-1 (Table 3)

pyrolysis.q: What functional group and vibration mode does Table 3 assign to the CH4 peaks, and at what wavenumbers?
pyrolysis.expect: C-H stretching vibration; 3014 cm-1 in air, 3016 cm-1 in nitrogen (Table 3)

pyrolysis.q: What loss on ignition did the extracted kerogen have, and what does the national standard require?
pyrolysis.expect: 88%; the standard requires an LOI greater than 75% (sec. 2.3.3)

pyrolysis.q: In the thermogravimetric tests, what sample mass, heating rates, final temperature and purge-gas flow rate were used?
pyrolysis.expect: about 5 mg; 5, 10 and 15 C/min; room temperature to 800 C; purge gas 50 mL/min (protective N2 20 mL/min) (sec. 2.3.2)
pyrolysis.trap: the STA test's 10 mg and 10 C/min

pyrolysis.q: By how many degrees does the maximum of the H2 signal occur earlier under air than under nitrogen?
pyrolysis.expect: about 120 C: maximum near 330 C in air vs near 450 C in nitrogen (sec. 3.3.1)
pyrolysis.trap: the 50 C earlier onset of mass loss

pyrolysis.q: At what heating rate and with what sample mass was the experiment run whose evolved gases were analysed by FTIR and MS?
pyrolysis.expect: the STA-FTIR-MS test on extracted kerogen: about 10 mg at 10 C/min to 800 C (sec. 2.3.4)
pyrolysis.trap: the TGA's 5 mg at 5, 10 and 15 C/min

pyrolysis.q: Why did the principal mass-loss region of kerogen begin about 50 C later under air than under nitrogen?
pyrolysis.expect: premise false: it began about 50 C EARLIER under air (abstract; sec. 3.1)

pyrolysis.q: Why were the apparent activation energies obtained under air higher than those under nitrogen?
pyrolysis.expect: premise false: under air they were LOWER over much of the conversion range (sec. 3.2); the paper also cautions they are not comparable intrinsic barriers

pyrolysis.q: What are the carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen and sulfur contents (ultimate analysis) of the Maoming oil shale sample?
pyrolysis.expect: not reported: the paper says sample-specific ultimate analysis was not available; only TOC 3.78 wt% is given (sec. 2.1)
pyrolysis.trap: inventing values or giving TOC as carbon content

co2-capture.q: In Table 1, what are the viscosities before and after absorption, and the CO2 loading, of the [TEPAH][ATA]/H2O system?
co2-capture.expect: 2.33 mPa s before, 5.44 mPa s after, loading 1.07 mol/mol; no phase separation (Table 1)

co2-capture.q: Among the absorbents compared in Table 2, which has the highest CO2 loading, and at what temperature was it measured?
What loading and viscosity does Table 2 list for the [DBAE][Im] ionic liquid?
co2-capture.expect: 0.82 mol/mol and 82.35 mPa s, at 313.15 K (Long et al.) (Table 2)

co2-capture.q: At the optimal desorption conditions, what regeneration efficiency was reached, and after five absorption-desorption cycles what remained?
co2-capture.expect: 94.7% at 393.15 K and 80 min; 88.6% of the initial value after five cycles (sec. 3.2)

co2-capture.q: How was [TEPAH][ATA] synthesized: amounts of TEPA and ATA, solvent, stirring time and evaporation temperature?
co2-capture.expect: 0.0125 mol TEPA and 0.0125 mol ATA in 30 mL ethanol/water (4:1 v/v), stirred 12 h at room temperature, rotary evaporated at 60 C under vacuum (sec. 2.2)

co2-capture.q: By what factor does the viscosity of neat [TEPAH][ATA] before absorption exceed that of the [TEPAH][ATA]/NPA/H2O system before absorption?
How does the CO2 loading of this work's absorbent compare with that of the conventional AMP/MEA/H2O system, as a ratio?
co2-capture.expect: about 3.6 times: 1.79 vs 0.5 mol/mol, both at 303.15 K (Table 2)

co2-capture.q: Why did the CO2-rich phase occupy about 72% of the total volume after saturation?
co2-capture.expect: premise false: the rich phase was only 28% of the volume (yet held over 96% of the absorbed CO2) (abstract)

co2-capture.q: Why did extending desorption at 393.15 K from 80 to 100 min raise the regeneration efficiency well above 94.7%?
co2-capture.expect: premise false: extending to 100 min did not improve regeneration efficiency; desorption was likely complete within 80 min (sec. 3.2)

co2-capture.q: What regeneration energy, in GJ per tonne of CO2, does the [TEPAH][ATA]/NPA/H2O absorbent require?
co2-capture.expect: not reported for this system; 3.7 GJ/t (MEA) and 1.23 GJ/t ([IPDAH][Im], Zheng et al.) are other systems from the literature
co2-capture.trap: giving 1.23 or 3.7 as this work's value

crystallization.q: At RH of about 59% and an evaporation temperature of 34 C, what share of droplets formed single crystals without the magnetic field and with it?
crystallization.trap: the 31 C row (11.8 / 26.7) or the coffee-ring column

crystallization.q: Which sample in Table 6 has the largest lattice constant, and under what evaporation conditions was it grown?
crystallization.expect: crystal 6: a = 6.574041(2) A, 30-31 C, zero field, RH about 33% (delta T = 1 C) (Table 6)

crystallization.q: At RH of about 11% and 28 C under the applied magnetic field, what share of droplets formed coffee rings and what was the average ring diameter?
What droplet volume was dispensed, and on what size of substrate?
crystallization.expect: 5 uL droplets on 5 mm x 5 mm silicon substrates (Experimental Setup)

crystallization.q: At RH of about 33% and 28 C, by how many percentage points did the share of coffee-ring deposits change when the magnetic field was applied?
crystallization.expect: +40 points: 40.0% zero field to 80% with the field (Table 3)

crystallization.q: How many of the droplets tested at RH of about 33% and 34 C without a magnetic field formed single crystals?
What radiation, scan range, step size and scan speed were used for powder X-ray diffraction?
crystallization.expect: Cu K-alpha; 2-100 degrees 2-theta; 0.01 degree steps; 20 degrees/min (Characterization Techniques)

crystallization.q: Which saturated salt solution set the humidity at which single crystals were most frequent?
crystallization.expect: sodium bromide: single crystals become more frequent at RH about 59%, which saturated NaBr maintained (LiCl 11%, MgCl2 33%) (Experimental Setup; Results)

crystallization.q: Why did the static magnetic field promote single-crystal formation at high humidity?
crystallization.expect: premise false: no measurable field effect; single crystals become more frequent at RH 59% independent of the applied field (abstract; Discussion)

crystallization.q: What contact angle did the sodium chlorate droplets make with the silicon substrate?
crystallization.expect: not reported (contact angle appears only in a cited reference title)

heat-transfer.q: What share of myristic acid (C14:0) did this work measure in macaw palm almond oil, and what did Goncalves and Amaral report?
According to Table 2, what kinematic viscosity at 40 C and what melting temperature does Jatropha curcas oil have?
heat-transfer.expect: 39.72 mm2/s at 40 C; melting temperature 35 C (Gomna et al.) (Table 2)

heat-transfer.q: What operating temperature and thermal conductivity does Table 2 give for Therminol VP-1?
What extraction yield and acid value did the macaw palm almond oil have?
In the Soxhlet extraction, how much hexane and how much almond were used per unit, and for how long at what temperature?
heat-transfer.expect: 125 mL hexane for about 17 g almond (about 1:7.3 m/v), about 5 h at about 70 C (sec. on oil extraction)
heat-transfer.trap: the 60 C oven used to evaporate hexane

heat-transfer.q: What is the total share of saturated fatty acids in this work's macaw palm almond oil?
heat-transfer.trap: leaving out minor acids or adding unsaturated ones

heat-transfer.q: For the fatty acid that dominates this work's macaw oil, what share did Goncalves report?
Why did thermogravimetric analysis show the macaw oil to be stable up to about 450 C?
heat-transfer.expect: premise false: measurable degradation began around 300 C, so continuous operation should stay below about 300 C (abstract; TGA section)

heat-transfer.q: Why was the acid value of this work's oil higher than every literature value for macaw oil that the paper compares?
heat-transfer.expect: premise false: 3.44 mg KOH/g is slightly lower than Goncalves (3.49) and much lower than Melo (12.24) and Amaral (12.8)

heat-transfer.q: What thermal conductivity (W/m K) did this work measure for macaw palm almond oil?
heat-transfer.expect: not determined: the paper says it could not determine thermal conductivity because of reproducibility limits; Table 2 shows '-'

heat-transfer.q: What specific heat capacity (J/g K) does the paper give for macaw palm almond oil?
heat-transfer.expect: not given: Table 2 shows '-' and the text says the calorific capacity was not determined in this work (Amaral's calorific value 4739 kcal/kg is a different quantity)
heat-transfer.trap: Jatropha's 1.92 or the 4739 kcal/kg calorific value

techno-economic.q: For MgSO4 draw solution with wastewater feed, what decay rate k, initial decay rate k0 and cumulative flux loss RCL does Table 3 report?
What PCOD, Kfoul and PCOD/Kfoul values are predicted for the MgSO4 draw solution?
techno-economic.expect: PCOD 0.185 L m-2 h-1, Kfoul 0.0405 L m-2 h-1, PCOD/Kfoul 4.58 (Table 7)

techno-economic.q: What project lifetime, discount rate and membrane service life were assumed in the techno-economic analysis?
What COD and osmotic pressure did the municipal wastewater feed have?
How much of each salt was dissolved per litre to make the three draw solutions, and to what osmotic pressure?
techno-economic.expect: NaCl 35.0 g/L, MgSO4.7H2O 71.8 g/L, sodium acetate 79.4 g/L, each to 30 bar at 25 C (sec. 2.2)

techno-economic.q: For sodium acetate, by what factor did the flux decay rate k increase when the feed switched from deionized water to wastewater?
By what factor is the levelized cost of water with MgSO4 higher than with NaCl?
For the draw/feed combination with the largest cumulative flux loss, what was the initial decay rate k0?
Why did replacing deionized water with real wastewater as the feed increase the water flux?
techno-economic.expect: premise false: wastewater REDUCED Jw by 8.1-46.2% depending on the draw solution (abstract)

techno-economic.q: Why was sodium acetate the most economically viable draw solution?
techno-economic.expect: premise false: NaCl was (LCOW USD 1.04/m3); sodium acetate USD 1.74/m3, near MgSO4's 1.75 (abstract; Conclusions)

techno-economic.q: What water contact angle did the CTA membrane have?
techno-economic.expect: not reported (Table 1 gives A, B, S and area only)

fluidized-bed.q: According to Table 3, how much Na (wt %) is on the silica sand surface and in the agglomerate neck structure?
fluidized-bed.expect: 0.00 wt % on silica sand; 32.61 wt % in the agglomerate (38.31 at.%) (Table 3)
fluidized-bed.trap: the at.% columns or the P/Fe rows

fluidized-bed.q: Which runs in the experimental matrix vary the bed particle size, and to what sizes?
fluidized-bed.expect: runs 6 and 7: 545 um and 775 um (all other runs 650 um) (Table 2)

fluidized-bed.q: What carbon content does Table 1 give for polypropylene and for the sewage sludge?
By what factor does the Fe content (wt %) of the agglomerate neck exceed that of the silica sand?
How often were feed packages added to the bed, and what did each package weigh?
fluidized-bed.expect: one package every 20 s; 2.45 g per package (sec. 2.1, 2.2)

fluidized-bed.q: How was fly ash sampled: how often, for how long each time, and following which standard?
fluidized-bed.expect: every 4 min, each sampling lasting 2 min, based on U.S. EPA Method 5 (sec. 2.2)

fluidized-bed.q: In the run of the experimental matrix with the highest incineration temperature, what gas velocity and P/Fe/Na ratio were used?
Why did raising the P share from 0.4 to 0.6 at a P/Fe/Na ratio with Fe = 5 lengthen the defluidization time?
fluidized-bed.expect: premise false: 0.6/5/1 gave a SHORTER defluidization time than 0.4/5/1; high P weakened Fe's inhibitory effect (abstract; sec. 3.2)

fluidized-bed.q: Why was the Cu emission concentration higher than that of Pb?
fluidized-bed.expect: premise false: Cu was LOWER than Pb, because of its higher melting and boiling points (abstract)

fluidized-bed.q: What minimum fluidization velocity, in m/s, was measured for the 650 um silica sand bed?
fluidized-bed.expect: not reported as a number: Umf was measured with a water manometer and runs used 1.3 Umf, but no value in m/s is given
